title: Budgeted warmstart temporal prefill + quant-compat signer and telemetry adapter
author: Priya Shankar
description:
Motivation: Tenant warmstarts and prefill behavior have been a major driver of cold-start unit cost for bursty workloads. Existing prefill is static and either underprovisions (latency spikes) or overprovisions (wasted tokens). This change introduces a temporal prefill controller that budgets warmstart work across short time windows and a lightweight quant-compat signer to ensure model-variant compatibility when falling back to compact quantized binaries.

What this PR does (high level):
- Temporal prefill controller: adds a controller that tracks recent cold-starts per-tenant and spreads prefill KV population across a configurable window (default 30s) to reduce token waste while preserving tail latency SLOs.
- Budgeted warmstart policy: exposes tenant-level warmstart budgets (tokens/sec and token-cap) and a budget allocator that prioritizes requests by SLA tier and recent activity.
- Quant-compat signer: a deterministic metadata signer embedded in model artifacts and runtime that asserts compatibility between compact quant artifacts and runtime kernels; runtime will use the signer to decide safe in-place fallback to quant variant.
- Telemetry adapter: new telemetry shim that emits per-tenant warmstart budget usage, temporal spread histograms, and quant-fallback decision traces to the existing metrics/traces pipeline.
- Backwards-compatible runtime changes: runtime checks are additive; operator can opt-in to budgeted warmstarts via config flags.

Testing & CI: 
- Unit test suite (go test ./...): passed locally and in CI (flaky DB test re-run once)
- Integration: lightweight smoke run in perf-canary environment; validated tail latency reductions on synthetic bursty workload (see attached perf artifacts)
- Linting: go vet/gofmt/lint passed

Backward compatibility & rollout: 
- Feature is behind `prefill.temporal.enabled` and `prefill.quant_signer.enabled`. Defaults: both disabled for Private installer and enabled in hosted experimental for opt-in customers.
- No breaking API changes to public Redwood API. Config proto change adds fields with defaults.

Release notes (short): 
"Introduce budgeted temporal warmstarts to reduce cold-start unit cost for bursty tenants; add quant-compat signer to enable safer fallbacks to compact quant artifacts; include telemetry for warmstart budgets and prefill spread histograms."

Follow-ups planned:

- A CLI dry-run tool to simulate budgeted prefill economics per-tenant.

Link to design doc: https://linear.app/company/issue/ENG-4921/temporal-prefill-and-budgeted-warmstart

discussion:
Reviewer Daniel Kim: Asked for stronger invariants in budget allocator to avoid starvation for bursty high-priority tenants; requested additional unit test covering simultaneous bursts across 3 tenants.
Author (Priya): Implemented a weighted priority queue and added the requested test (tests/integration/prefill_temporal_test.go). Commented with explanation of priority decay parameters and why they were chosen.
Rae Cho: Flagged that quant-compat signer should produce stable signatures across builds; asked for explicit hashing algorithm and a migration plan for existing artifacts.
Author: Added signer tests and documented the algorithm (SHA256 over artifact manifest + version salt). Added a migration helper that logs unverifiable artifacts and falls back to byte-for-byte control plane verification when enabled.
Miguel Alvarez: Requested telemetry labels to include tenant_tier and region; noted that histograms currently use coarse buckets.
Author: Adjusted telemetry adapter to emit tenant_tier and region tags and refined histogram buckets based on perf-canary feedback.
Approvals: After fixes, reviewers approved (Daniel Kim, Rae Cho). CI passing and merge was performed via squash merge.
Notes: One transient CI failure on integration job (timeout); re-run succeeded. Security review: small concerns about signer secret handling — signer uses public asymmetric keys embedded in runtime; private signing done only in artifact publish path. Security sign-off given by security@redwood on 2024-11-19.
